title: Labels
definition: The `<label>` element represents a caption for an item in a user interface, specifically tying text to a specific form input.
simpleExplanation: If you just type text next to a checkbox, clicking the text does nothing. If you wrap that text in a `<label>` and link it to the checkbox, clicking the text will magically check the box! This makes forms vastly easier to use, especially on mobile devices where checkboxes are tiny.
realWorldExample: Every properly built form on the internet uses labels. Without them, screen readers don't know what an input box is for, and blind users won't know what to type.
useCases: Improving click targets for small inputs like radio buttons

basic: How do you link a `<label>` to an `<input>`?
intermediate: What happens if you click a properly linked label?

answers.question: How to link them?
answers.answer: Give the `<input>` a unique `id` attribute. Then, give the `<label>` a `for` attribute with the exact same value. (e.g., `<label for="email">` and `<input id="email">`).

answers.question: What happens when clicked?
answers.answer: The browser automatically transfers focus to the linked input. For text boxes, the cursor appears. For checkboxes/radios, they toggle on or off.

codeExample: I am just text next to an input. Clicking me does nothing.
